content: youtube-dl-exec (latest 3.1.9) is still actively published; yt-dlp-exec is a fork that defaults to the yt-dlp binary instead of the abandoned youtube-dl and works as a drop-in replacement. Since youtube-dl itself is far less maintained than yt-dlp, yt-dlp-exec (or configuring youtube-dl-exec to point at a yt-dlp binary) is the recommended wrapper. Both are thin argv wrappers around the actual yt-dlp binary, which must be present on the host (Python-based tool), a key hosting/deployment implication.
